1.1 Central idea

This plan uses a direct true-objective minimax local optimizer with a feasible linear-programming model-step construction. The main search variable is still the original step vector h, and every accepted new vector is scored only by the official discrete objective

C5(h) = max_{lag in all 2n-1 lags} dx * sum_i h_i (1 - h_{i+lag(i)}), dx = 2/n,

where the lag formula and summation limits are exactly those produced by np.correlate(h, 1-h, mode="full"). No log-sum-exp smoothing surrogate is used as the accepted objective; no globally convex relaxation or claimed optimal global method is implied.

The primary optimization envelope is a trust-region linearization of all, or many if large, lag-correlation scores. At the current feasible h, for selected lag scores f_l(h), the next numerical model is affine

f_l(h+p) approximately f_l(h) + grad_l(h) dot p,

subject to p sum p = 0 and h_i+p_i in [0,1]. A small trust radius bounds the first-order model. Solving the resulting linear program

minimize tau
subject f_l(h) + grad_l dot p <= tau for selected active/influential lags l,
sum_i p_i = 0,
lower/upper bounds and trust-radius bounds,

produces a feasible bulk direction p that is expected to reduce the maximum correlation under the local linearized model. The candidate is never evaluated using the prediction: a one-dimensional exact line search is performed along h + alpha p, using the exact public correlation evaluator, and only true objective decreases are accepted. This exact acceptance makes the method safe for a nonconvex objective: if the linear model is inaccurate because the exact function is quadratic/bilinear, the step is simply rejected and the trust radius shrinks.

This differs substantively from the supplied parent program and from the supplied previous strategies:

- The supplied parent program used high-beta log-sum-exp smoothing and SLSQP under a nonconvex constrained optimization, followed by rounded/reprojected filtering. The main work is a convex bulk minimax linear model plus exact line-search filtering, not a smooth-max penalty or pair-coordinate line search.
- The move is a full bulk direction satisfying the sum constraint in the linear model. It is not the pairwise mass-transfer pair-line method from the earlier strategies, although feasibility repair and auxiliary global perturbations are allowed.
- The algorithm is used as a local descent engine and then embedded inside random-perturbation restarts, symmetric/complement transform seeds, and resolution transfers. The primary novelty in the code is therefore convex-approximation direction finding under exact true-objective acceptance.

The parent is smooth and nonsmooth-objective optimized, but Minimize is not globally guaranteed. The target reduction is small: about 0.00039 from 0.381190. Thus a reliable local polishing mechanism that can construct supporting descent directions from all active lag constraints is worthwhile. A full LP direction uses the local active constraint set collectively, reducing a single maximum in an L-infinity model at each step. If several active lags are in tension with each other, a pair-update or subgradient move may fail to balance them; the LP direction explicitly balances the selected local maxima.

The side mechanisms—small random perturbation restarts, h-to-reverse-complement blends, and resolution transfer around parent n—address local-optimum and discretization effects.
